claim: In 0-2hAEL embryos, category two small RNAs (endo-siRNA + piRNA) constituted >50% of the small RNA population.
source: In 0-2hAEL embryos, category two small RNAs constituted >50% of the small RNA population, consistent with the large amount of maternally deposited piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) produced from various transposons (Brennecke et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from small RNA library analysis shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: The large amount of category two small RNAs in 0-2hAEL embryos is consistent with maternally deposited piRNAs produced from various transposons.
source: In 0-2hAEL embryos, category two small RNAs constituted >50% of the small RNA population, consistent with the large amount of maternally deposited piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) produced from various transposons (Brennecke et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Brennecke et al., 2008 and is consistent with the observed data.

claim: The fraction of category two small RNAs continuously declined until 12-18hAEL.
source: The fraction of category two small RNAs continuously declined until 12-18hAEL, with a concomitant increase of the miRNA fraction.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: There was a concomitant increase of the miRNA fraction as category two small RNAs declined.
source: The fraction of category two small RNAs continuously declined until 12-18hAEL, with a concomitant increase of the miRNA fraction.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In 18-24hAEL, there was a reproducible increase of small RNAs derived from abundant ncRNAs.
source: In 18-24hAEL, we observed a reproducible increase of small RNAs derived from abundant ncRNAs.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Small RNAs derived from abundant ncRNAs in 18-24hAEL were mainly derived from rRNAs.
source: Closer inspection revealed that these small RNAs were mainly derived from rRNAs, and no specific size peaks were observed with this category of small RNAs in this time window (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: No specific size peaks were observed with rRNA-derived small RNAs in the 18-24hAEL time window.
source: Closer inspection revealed that these small RNAs were mainly derived from rRNAs, and no specific size peaks were observed with this category of small RNAs in this time window (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: rRNA-derived small RNAs may be degradation intermediates with no functionality.
source: These results suggested that rRNA-derived small RNAs may be degradation intermediates with no functionality, but the reason for this rapid increase of these fragments in this developmental stage is not known.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observation that these small RNAs lack specific size peaks.

claim: The reason for the rapid increase of rRNA-derived small RNA fragments in 18-24hAEL is not known.
source: These results suggested that rRNA-derived small RNAs may be degradation intermediates with no functionality, but the reason for this rapid increase of these fragments in this developmental stage is not known.
evidence: The authors explicitly state that the reason is unknown.

claim: A continuous increase of the total mature miRNA abundance was observed throughout embryogenesis.
source: We first analyzed the overall abundance of miRNAs after normalizing read counts against the spike-in counts (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1 Sheet 2). We observed a continuous increase of the total mature miRNA abundance throughout embryogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The continuous increase of total mature miRNA abundance throughout embryogenesis may be consistent with the notion that early embryos generally show relatively low miRNA activity and differentiated cells rely more strongly on miRNA-mediated mechanisms for gene regulation.
source: This may be consistent with the notion that early embryos generally show relatively low miRNA activity and differentiated cells rely more strongly on miRNA-mediated mechanisms for gene regulation (Lu et al., 2005; Kumar et al., 2007; Kumar et al., 2009; Suh et al., 2010; Ohnishi et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and is consistent with the observed data.

claim: A gradual decrease of the piRNA population was observed during embryogenesis.
source: On the other hand, we observed a gradual decrease of the piRNA population (Figure 1B; Supplementary file 1 Sheet 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The gradual decrease of the piRNA population was consistent with expression patterns of mRNAs encoding the piRNA pathway components with high levels in early embryos.
source: This was also consistent with expression patterns of mRNAs encoding the piRNA pathway components with high levels in early embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and largely restricted to gonads in late stages (Ishizu et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and citation to Ishizu et al., 2012.

claim: piRNA pathway components are largely restricted to gonads in late embryonic stages.
source: This was also consistent with expression patterns of mRNAs encoding the piRNA pathway components with high levels in early embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and largely restricted to gonads in late stages (Ishizu et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ishizu et al., 2012.

claim: The normalized miRNA expression values estimated by library analysis generally showed good agreement with Northern blotting results.
source: The normalized miRNA expression values estimated by library analysis generally showed good agreement with our Northern blotting results (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 2), indicating that our sequencing analysis accurately estimated levels of miRNA expression relative to the amount of total RNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of data from Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The sequencing analysis accurately estimated levels of miRNA expression relative to the amount of total RNA.
source: The normalized miRNA expression values estimated by library analysis generally showed good agreement with our Northern blotting results (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 2), indicating that our sequencing analysis accurately estimated levels of miRNA expression relative to the amount of total RNA.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the good agreement between library analysis and Northern blotting results.

claim: The amount of total RNA per embryo stayed relatively constant throughout embryogenesis.
source: We found that the amount of total RNA per embryo stayed relatively constant throughout embryogenesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Library analysis results using spike-in normalization reflect the relative abundance of each miRNA species per embryo.
source: Therefore, we believe that our library analysis results using spike-in normalization reflect the relative abundance of each miRNA species per embryo (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that total RNA per embryo stays constant.

claim: Cluster 1 included 15 miRNAs that showed the highest expression levels in early stages.
source: Cluster 1 included 15 miRNAs that showed the highest expression levels in early stages.
evidence: The claim is supported by k-means clustering analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The majority of miRNA genes in Cluster 1 were maternally deposited miRNAs with weak zygotic expression.
source: The majority of miRNA genes in this group were maternally deposited miRNAs with weak zygotic expression (Lee et al., 2014; Marco, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2014 and Marco, 2015.

claim: The rapid decrease of maternal mature miRNA species was consistent with Wispy-mediated degradation of maternal miRNAs.
source: The rapid decrease of maternal mature miRNA species was consistent with Wispy-mediated degradation of maternal miRNAs as reported previously (Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lee et al., 2014 and is consistent with the observed data.

claim: Cluster 4 included 6 genes and showed detectable decrease in late stages.
source: Cluster 4 included 6 genes and showed detectable decrease in late stages.
evidence: The claim is supported by k-means clustering analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The observation that Cluster 4 miRNAs decrease in late stages suggested that these miRNAs are relatively unstable.
source: This observation suggested that these miRNAs are relatively unstable, and the small number of genes in this category was consistent with the conclusion in previous cell culture-based studies that a small subset of miRNAs is degraded relatively quickly (Duffy et al., 2015; Marzi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed decrease in late stages and is consistent with previous studies.

claim: The small number of genes in Cluster 4 was consistent with the conclusion in previous cell culture-based studies that a small subset of miRNAs is degraded relatively quickly.
source: This observation suggested that these miRNAs are relatively unstable, and the small number of genes in this category was consistent with the conclusion in previous cell culture-based studies that a small subset of miRNAs is degraded relatively quickly (Duffy et al., 2015; Marzi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Duffy et al., 2015 and Marzi et al., 2016.

claim: The majority (75.8%; 66 out of 87 genes) of genes belonged to clusters 2 and 3 that showed increasing trends throughout embryogenesis.
source: The majority (75.8%; 66 out of 87 genes) of genes belonged to clusters 2 and 3 that showed increasing trends throughout embryogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by k-means clustering analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The increase in expression level is a general trend for many miRNA genes in fly embryos.
source: This indicated that the increase in the expression level is a general trend for many miRNA genes in fly embryos, and that the increase in the bulk miRNA abundance was not caused by a small number of miRNA species.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the majority of miRNA genes show increasing trends.

claim: The increase in the bulk miRNA abundance was not caused by a small number of miRNA species.
source: This indicated that the increase in the expression level is a general trend for many miRNA genes in fly embryos, and that the increase in the bulk miRNA abundance was not caused by a small number of miRNA species.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the majority of miRNA genes show increasing trends.

claim: The AGO1 protein level was lower in very early embryos (0–2h and 2–4h).
source: Coincidentally, the AGO1 protein level was also lower in very early embryos (Figure 1—figure supplements 3B, 0–2h and 2–4h lanes).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The AGO1 protein level may be a limiting factor that determines the bulk miRNA abundance.
source: This may suggest that the AGO1 protein level may be a limiting factor that determines the bulk miRNA abundance.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the correlation between AGO1 protein levels and miRNA abundance.

claim: The lower level of mature miRNAs may trigger degradation of apo-AGO1, as observed in tissues depleted of miRNA processing factors.
source: Alternatively, the lower level of mature miRNAs may trigger degradation of apo-AGO1, as observed in tissues depleted of miRNA processing factors (Smibert et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by citation to Smibert et al., 2013.

claim: The large difference of the total miRNA levels (eight times increase from 0-2hAEL to 18-24hAEL) estimated by spike-in normalization underscores the importance of the selection of normalization methods.
source: The large difference of the total miRNA levels (eight times increase from 0-2hAEL to 18-24hAEL) estimated by our method underscores the importance of the selection of normalization methods, as the conventional RPM (reads per million) normalization method generally disregards the change in the size of small RNA population.
evidence: The claim is supported by the observed data and comparison of normalization methods.

claim: The conventional RPM (reads per million) normalization method generally disregards the change in the size of small RNA population.
source: The large difference of the total miRNA levels (eight times increase from 0-2hAEL to 18-24hAEL) estimated by our method underscores the importance of the selection of normalization methods, as the conventional RPM (reads per million) normalization method generally disregards the change in the size of small RNA population.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about RPM normalization.

claim: Pri-miRNA species (or introns in the case of miRNAs residing in introns of protein-coding mRNAs) are believed to have much shorter half-lives compared to mature mRNAs or mature miRNAs.
source: Pri-miRNA species (or introns in the case of miRNAs residing in introns of protein-coding mRNAs) are believed to have much shorter half-lives compared to mature mRNAs or mature miRNAs (Gaidatzis et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2015; Nojima et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gaidatzis et al., 2015; Chang et al., 2015; Nojima et al., 2015.

claim: Transient peaks of the pri-miRNA levels were often observed, suggesting that miRNA transcription is activated generally in short time-windows.
source: Consistent with this notion, transient peaks of the pri-miRNA levels were often observed, suggesting that miRNA transcription is activated generally in short time-windows (Figure 1C, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and is inferred from the observation of transient peaks.

claim: For miRNAs in clusters 2 and 3 that showed the highest mature miRNA levels in the last time window, their corresponding primary miRNAs generally exhibited expression peaks in earlier time windows while mature miRNA remained present for at least several hours.
source: For example, even for the miRNAs in clusters 2 and 3 that showed the highest mature miRNA levels in the last time window, their corresponding primary miRNAs generally exhibited expression peaks in earlier time windows while mature miRNA remained present for at least several hours.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The change rate of mature miRNA level per unit of time should be determined by two factors: new synthesis and degradation.
source: The change rate of mature miRNA level per unit of time (hereafter 'miRNA change rate') should be determined by two factors: new synthesis and degradation.
evidence: The claim is based on logical reasoning about factors affecting miRNA levels.

claim: The level of transcription would be the primary determinant of the miRNA synthesis rate.
source: For simplicity, we approximated the model based on the following two assumptions: the level of transcription would be the primary determinant of the miRNA synthesis rate and the amount of mature miRNA that is degraded at a given moment would be proportional to the amount of miRNA products present at the moment.
evidence: The claim is an assumption made for the multiple linear regression analysis.

claim: The amount of mature miRNA that is degraded at a given moment would be proportional to the amount of miRNA products present at the moment.
source: For simplicity, we approximated the model based on the following two assumptions: the level of transcription would be the primary determinant of the miRNA synthesis rate and the amount of mature miRNA that is degraded at a given moment would be proportional to the amount of miRNA products present at the moment.
evidence: The claim is an assumption made for the multiple linear regression analysis.

claim: The change rates of mature miRNA could be generally accurately predicted (r2 = 0.81) based on initial miRNA level and pri-miRNA abundance.
source: When we tested the correlation between the predicted and observed change rates for all time windows of all miRNAs, we found that the change rates could be generally accurately predicted (r2 = 0.81; Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: For the majority of miRNAs, the production rate per pri-miRNA molecule as well as the degradation rate of mature miRNAs were relatively constant throughout embryogenesis.
source: This suggested that, for the majority of miRNAs, the production rate per pri-miRNA molecule as well as the degradation rate of mature miRNAs were relatively constant throughout embryogenesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the accurate prediction of miRNA change rates.

claim: The predicted change rate tended to be higher than the observed data in early time windows.
source: Nevertheless, when we analyzed the prediction accuracy in each window, we observed a trend where the predicted change rate tended to be higher than the observed data in early time windows (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Mature miRNAs may have been less efficiently processed from pri-miRNAs in early embryos.
source: This may mean that mature miRNAs were less efficiently processed from pri-miRNAs in early embryos.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observation that predicted change rates were higher than observed in early time windows.

claim: Pri-miRNA degradation might be slower in early time windows, leading to an overestimation of transcriptional activity.
source: It is also possible that pri-miRNA degradation might be slower in these windows, leading to an overestimation of transcriptional activity.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observation that predicted change rates were higher than observed in early time windows.

claim: The small amount of maternal miRNAs and their rapid degradation might contribute to inaccurate prediction in early time windows.
source: Although we excluded miRNAs that are deposited as maternal miRNAs at high levels from this analysis, the small amount of maternal miRNAs and their rapid degradation (Lee et al., 2014) might also contribute to this inaccurate prediction in this window.
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by citation to Lee et al., 2014.

claim: In time windows other than early embryos, the distribution of prediction errors did not show clear trends, suggesting that the kinetics of miRNA production/degradation stayed relatively constant in these windows.
source: In other time windows, the distribution of prediction errors did not show clear trends, suggesting that the kinetics of miRNA production/degradation stayed relatively constant in these windows (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E and is inferred from the lack of clear trends.

claim: Integrated analysis of mature and primary miRNAs confirmed the general assumption that transcription level is important for determining the expression patterns of mature miRNAs.
source: Our integrated analysis of mature and primary miRNAs confirmed the general assumption that transcription level is important for determining the expression patterns of mature miRNAs and suggested that global miRNA production and degradation rates are relatively constant during embryogenesis except for early embryos.
evidence: The claim is supported by the results of the integrated analysis.

claim: Global miRNA production and degradation rates are relatively constant during embryogenesis except for early embryos.
source: Our integrated analysis of mature and primary miRNAs confirmed the general assumption that transcription level is important for determining the expression patterns of mature miRNAs and suggested that global miRNA production and degradation rates are relatively constant during embryogenesis except for early embryos.
evidence: The claim is supported by the results of the integrated analysis.

claim: Individual predicted values may not be accurate due to the inaccuracy of sequence-based quantification and the relatively low time-resolution of the time course.
source: However, we note that individual predicted values may not be accurate due to the inaccuracy of sequence-based quantification and the relatively low time-resolution of our time course.
evidence: The authors acknowledge limitations of their analysis.

claim: It is possible that there are a small number of individual miRNAs that are regulated post-transcriptionally in a time-window specific manner in embryos.
source: In addition, it is also possible that there are a small number of individual miRNAs that are regulated post-transcriptionally in a time-window specific manner in embryos.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the limitations of the analysis.

claim: The identity of 5' end nucleotide of the guide RNA influences the interactions between the guide RNA and the MID domain of Argonaute with 5'-uridine (5'-U) showing the highest affinity among the four nucleotides.
source: The identity of 5' end nucleotide of the guide RNA influences the interactions between the guide RNA and the MID domain of Argonaute with 5'-uridine (5'-U) showing the highest affinity among the four nucleotides (Frank et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Frank et al., 2010.

claim: Mature miRNAs are believed to be protected by Argonaute proteins from degradation.
source: Since mature miRNAs are believed to be protected by Argonaute proteins from degradation, we wondered if the identity of the 5' nucleotide could also influence the stability of miRNAs.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about miRNA-Argonaute interactions.

claim: The coefficient values associated with the mature miRNA abundance were generally higher with mature miRNAs carrying 5'-U than those carrying other 5'-nucleotides (p=0.01, one-tailed Kolmogorov-Smirnov test).
source: Nevertheless, when the values were compared between groups of miRNAs with 5'-U and other 5'-nucleotides, we observed a trend whereby the coefficient values associated with the mature miRNA abundance were generally higher with mature miRNAs carrying 5'-U than those carrying other 5'-nucleotides (p=0.01, one-tailed Kolmogorov-Smirnov test; mean5'U=-0.0016, meannon-5'U=-0.088; median5'U=0.013, mediannon-5'U= -0.087) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: One may expect the trend of higher coefficient values for 5'-U miRNAs if miRNAs with 5'-U are more stable than miRNAs with other nucleotides at the 5' end.
source: One may expect this trend if miRNAs with 5'-U are more stable than miRNAs with other nucleotides at the 5' end.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observed trend.

claim: The miR-283 A-to-U mutant exhibited a slightly (~20%) but reproducible stabilization compared to wild-type miR-283 with average half-lives of 14.9 and 18.3 hr for wild-type and A-to-U mutant, respectively (p<0.02, paired one-tailed t-test).
source: We observed a slight (~20%) but reproducible stabilization of the mutated miR-283 with average half-lives of 14.9 and 18.3 hr for wild-type and A-to-U mutant, respectively (p<0.02, paired one-tailed t-test).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: The miR-283 star strand was present at very low levels compared to the mature strand, confirming that the miRNA stability measurements reflect the half-lives of mature miRNAs that are already loaded to the Argonaute complex.
source: The miR-283 star strand was present at very low levels compared to the mature strand, confirming that the miRNA stability measurements reflect the half-lives of mature miRNAs that are already loaded to the Argonaute complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Changing the 5'-As of two other miRNAs to 5'-Us resulted in stabilizing effects similar to the miR-283 A-to-U mutant.
source: When we changed the 5'-As of two other miRNAs to 5'-Us, we observed stabilizing effects similar to the miR-283 A-to-U mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mutating 5'-A to 5'-G did not significantly affect the stability of miRNAs.
source: On the other hand, mutating 5'-A to 5'-G did not significantly affect the stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Significant stabilization was observed when the mature miRNA 5' ends were changed to 5'-C, which is the preferred 5' nucleotide by the Drosophila siRNA Argonaute AGO2.
source: We also observed significant stabilization when the mature miRNA 5' ends were changed to 5'-C, which is the preferred 5' nucleotide by the Drosophila siRNA Argonaute AGO2 (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2) (Ghildiyal et al., 2010; Czech et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2, and citations to Ghildiyal et al., 2010 and Czech et al., 2009.

claim: The results revealed the importance of 5' nucleotides in stabilizing mature miRNAs, in addition to their previously characterized roles in miRNA loading to Argonautes.
source: The results revealed the importance of 5' nucleotides in stabilizing mature miRNAs, in addition to their previously characterized roles in miRNA loading to Argonautes (Meister, 2013; Frank et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to Meister, 2013 and Frank et al., 2010.

claim: miRNA genes often form clusters in the genome and those clustered miRNAs are believed to be co-transcribed as polycistronic units.
source: miRNA genes often form clusters in the genome and those clustered miRNAs are believed to be co-transcribed as polycistronic units.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about miRNA gene organization.

claim: If the level of transcription is the major determinant of the miRNA expression levels, miRNAs within a cluster should show similar changes in their expression levels.
source: Therefore, if the level of transcription is the major determinant of the miRNA expression levels, miRNAs within a cluster should show similar changes in their expression levels.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the assumption that clustered miRNAs are co-transcribed.

claim: Several time windows were observed where miRNA cluster members showed distinct expression patterns.
source: Nevertheless, we observed several time windows where miRNA cluster members showed distinct expression patterns (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: From the 21 miRNA clusters in the D. melanogaster genome, 52 mature miRNA species derived from 13 miRNA clusters could be detected after removing multi-copy genes.
source: Overall, from the 21 miRNA clusters in the D. melanogaster genome (Kozomara and Griffiths-Jones, 2014), we could detect 52 mature miRNA species derived from 13 miRNA clusters after removing multi-copy genes (i.e. families with the same mature sequence) (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4 and citation to Kozomara and Griffiths-Jones, 2014.

claim: The majority of mature miRNA species from a single cluster showed similar expression patterns (adjusted p>0.01, one-way ANOVA analysis).
source: As expected, the majority of mature miRNA species from a single cluster showed similar expression patterns (adjusted p>0.01, one-way ANOVA analysis).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Four clusters exhibited significant differences in at least one time window.
source: However, four clusters exhibited significant differences in at least one time window (Figure 4, highlighted by red rectangles, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4 and Supplementary file 5.

claim: The results observed with clustered miRNAs suggested that a small number of miRNAs are regulated by additional mechanisms rather than simple regulation of transcriptional activity.
source: These results observed with clustered miRNAs suggested that a small number of miRNAs are regulated by additional mechanisms rather than simple regulation of transcriptional activity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that some cluster members show distinct expression patterns.

claim: The mir-317 cluster consists of three miRNAs (miR-317, miR-34 and miR-277).
source: This cluster consists of three miRNAs (miR-317, miR-34 and miR-277) and plays important roles during fly aging through multiple mechanisms including modulation of ecdysone signaling and branched-chain amino acid catabolism via the actions of miR-34 and miR-277, respectively (Liu et al., 2012; Esslinger et al., 2013; Xiong et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the mir-317 cluster.

claim: The mir-317 cluster plays important roles during fly aging through multiple mechanisms including modulation of ecdysone signaling and branched-chain amino acid catabolism via the actions of miR-34 and miR-277, respectively.
source: This cluster consists of three miRNAs (miR-317, miR-34 and miR-277) and plays important roles during fly aging through multiple mechanisms including modulation of ecdysone signaling and branched-chain amino acid catabolism via the actions of miR-34 and miR-277, respectively (Liu et al., 2012; Esslinger et al., 2013; Xiong et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2012; Esslinger et al., 2013; Xiong et al., 2016.

claim: Previous studies reported seemingly inconsistent results on mir-317 cluster miRNA expression levels, which showed up-regulation of miR-34 and down-regulation of miR-277 during aging.
source: However, previous studies reported seemingly inconsistent results on their expression levels, which showed up-regulation of miR-34 and down-regulation of miR-277 during aging (Liu et al., 2012; Esslinger et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2012 and Esslinger et al., 2013.

claim: Five major primary miRNA isoforms with combinations of alternative TSSs and TTSs were identified in the mir-317 locus.
source: We were able to identify five major primary miRNA isoforms with combinations of alternative TSSs and TTSs in this locus (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: One of the mir-317 pri-miRNA isoforms only covered the mir-277 hairpin, starting in downstream of the mir-317 hairpin and ending in upstream of the mir-34 hairpin.
source: Interestingly, one of the isoforms only covered the mir-277 hairpin, starting in downstream of the mir-317 hairpin and ending in upstream of the mir-34 hairpin.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The short mir-277-specific isoform was the main isoform expressed in embryos and its expression peak was seen at ~14–18 hAEL.
source: This short isoform was the main isoform expressed in embryos and its expression peak was seen at ~14–18 hAEL (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), coinciding with the time window where the significant difference between miR-277 and miR-317/–34 expression changes was observed (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 4.

claim: The expression peak of the short mir-277-specific isoform coincided with the time window where the significant difference between miR-277 and miR-317/–34 expression changes was observed.
source: This short isoform was the main isoform expressed in embryos and its expression peak was seen at ~14–18 hAEL (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), coinciding with the time window where the significant difference between miR-277 and miR-317/–34 expression changes was observed (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 4.

claim: In contrast to embryos, adult tissues use the long isoforms as the main primary mir-317 isoform.
source: In contrast to embryos, adult tissues use the long isoforms as the main primary mir-317 isoform.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Relative levels of miR-317/–34 compared to that of miR-277 in ovaries and testes were much higher than those in embryos, consistent with the long isoform expression.
source: Consistent with the long isoform expression, relative levels of miR-317/–34 compared to that of miR-277 in ovaries and testes were much higher than those in embryos (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The higher expression levels of miR-317 and −34 may imply that these two miRNA hairpins are more efficiently processed from pri-miRNAs than miR-277.
source: The higher expression levels of miR-317 and −34 may imply that these two miRNA hairpins are more efficiently processed from pri-miRNAs than miR-277.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observed expression patterns.

claim: Consistent changes in the histone modification status at alternative TSS sites support the idea that the alternative pri-miRNA isoforms were derived from alternative TSSs.
source: Supporting the idea that the alternative pri-miRNA isoforms were derived from alternative TSSs, we observed consistent changes in the histone modification status at these sites (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The authors favor the hypothesis that the relative levels of mir-317 cluster miRNAs could be altered by the selection of alternative TSS and TTS.
source: Although we do not formally exclude the possibility that the observed pri-miRNA isoforms may represent processing intermediates as seen in previous studies (Du et al., 2015), we favor the hypothesis that the relative levels of mir-317 cluster miRNAs could be altered by the selection of alternative TSS and TTS.
evidence: The authors state their preferred interpretation of the data.

claim: Expression of the mir-317 cluster miRNAs is controlled by the insect steroid hormone ecdysone.
source: Expression of the mir-317 cluster miRNAs is controlled by the insect steroid hormone ecdysone (Sempere et al., 2003; Ameres et al., 2010; Xiong et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sempere et al., 2003; Ameres et al., 2010; Xiong et al., 2016.

claim: In the embryonic Kc167 cells, both long (starting at TSS1/2) and short (starting at TSS3) pri-miRNA isoforms were expressed in the absence of ecdysone.
source: In the embryonic Kc167 cells, we found that both long (starting at TSS1/2) and short (starting at TSS3) pri-miRNA isoforms were expressed in the absence of ecdysone and showed intermediate ratios of mature miR-277 and mature miR-34/–317 levels compared to embryos (high miR-277) and adult tissues (low miR-277) (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: When Kc167 cells were treated with 20-hydroxyecdysone (20-HE), only the long transcripts starting at TSS1/2 were strongly down-regulated.
source: When Kc167 cells were treated with 20-hydroxyecdysone (20-HE), only the long transcripts starting at TSS1/2 were strongly down-regulated (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Consistent with the differential effects of ecdysone on the pri-mir-317-cluster isoforms, miR-317 and miR-34 decreased more strongly than miR-277 in Kc167 cells.
source: Consistent with the differential effects of ecdysone on the pri-mir-317-cluster isoforms, miR-317 and miR-34 decreased more strongly than miR-277 in Kc167 cells (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: A similar trend of differential miRNA decrease upon 20-HE treatment was observed in S2-R+ cells.
source: We observed a similar trend in another embryonic cell line, S2-R+ (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Embryos overexpressing miR-3/–309 exhibited defects in denticle organization.
source: When we plotted expression levels of the mir-309 cluster miRNAs in the eight time windows, we noticed that these miRNAs exhibited distinct rates of decrease (Figure 4). The results with elbow plot and k-means clustering analyses suggested that expression changes of miRNAs in this cluster could be divided into two groups, with one group consisting of miR-3 and miR-309 and the other containing miR-4, –5, −6 and −286 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). We calculated the half-lives of these miRNAs and miR-3/–309 showed ~3–10 times faster degradation rates compared to those of miR-4, –5, −6 and −286 (Figure 6B). The faster disappearance of miR-3 and miR-309 was confirmed by Northern blotting analysis, excluding the possibility of sequencing artifacts (Figure 6C and D). It was possible that the unstable miRNAs were not loaded to the Argonaute complex hence more susceptible to degradation by ribonucleases. Therefore, we examined whether the miRNAs were properly loaded to the major miRNA Argonaute AGO1 (Okamura et al., 2004), by precipitating the AGO1 complex from two time windows (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 2). We observed no obvious difference in the loading efficiency between stable (miR-4, –5, −6 and −286) and unstable (miR-3 and −309) miRNAs from this cluster. Furthermore, clear reduction of the mature miRNA species in the supernatant samples suggested that a large fraction of all the examined mature miRNAs were properly loaded to AGO1 (Figure 6E charts). Therefore, we concluded the difference in the reduction rate reflected the difference in the mature miRNA stability in the Argonaute complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7B.
